lead.headline: Treasury Yields Touch 5% and Fed Officials Back a December Hike as Stocks Slip, While China Extends the Tariff Truce to Jan. 10
lead.deck: Tuesday's inflation fallout dragged the Nasdaq down 0.74% and Nvidia down 5.5%, but oil fell to its lowest settlement since Aug. 31 and U.S. gas dipped below $4.

board_note: Figures as of Nov. 10 close unless noted (mortgage Nov. 6, Bitcoin Nov. 9); sources in each story.

stories.headline: Stocks Slip After the Inflation Report: S&P 500 Down 0.38%, Nasdaq Down 0.74%, and the 10-Year Yield Touches 5%
stories.deck: Tech led the decline as October's hotter-than-forecast prices pushed rate-hike bets and bond yields higher.
paras: The S&P 500 closed Tuesday at 7,520.93, down 0.38%, the Dow fell 0.30% to 52,231.89, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.74% to 25,065.88. All three had been on a two-day winning streak that the October consumer price report ended. About 61% of U.S. issues declined, and technology was the weakest sector, down 1.13%, while financials, energy and communication services were the leaders.

Bond yields did much of the damage. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped roughly 9 to 14 basis points depending on the source and sat at about 5.0%, with the two-year yield near 4.75%. One analyst quoted by TheStreet said money was moving out of AI stocks and into defensive areas such as healthcare. Chipmakers were a bright spot: AMD, Broadcom and Lam Research each gained more than 7%, even as Nvidia sank.
Wednesday is Veterans Day, so U.S. stock markets are open but the bond market is closed, which can mean thin trading in Treasuries.
money: Rising yields tend to lift rates on savings accounts, CDs and Treasury bills; it can pay to compare what your bank offers with top online accounts.
Index-fund investors saw a one-day dip; a decline of under 1% is routine, and a fixed monthly contribution schedule avoids the temptation to time the market.
Check how much of your portfolio is tied to a handful of AI-linked megacaps, since those have driven both the rallies and the recent swings.
Bond prices fall when yields rise; if you hold a bond fund, expect its price to move opposite to rates in the short term.

sources.t: Stock Market Today, Nov. 10, 2026 (TheStreet)
Dow, Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall on Nov. 10; oil and gold retreat (Eurasia Business News)
U.S. stocks decline as October CPI exceeds expectations; Nvidia drops 5.5% (KuCoin News)

stories.headline: Two Fed Officials Back More Hikes: A Quarter-Point Move in December Is Fully Priced In, With a Half-Point Still Possible
stories.deck: Governor Waller leans toward 0.25 point and would weigh 0.50; Dallas Fed's Logan says two more increases are needed.
stories.summary: CME FedWatch shows a 25-basis-point hike fully priced for Dec. 8-9 and about a 13.6% chance of 50; policy rate is 3.75-4.00%.
paras: After Tuesday's inflation report, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support at least a quarter-point rate increase at the December 8-9 meeting and would consider a half-point if price pressures worsen. Reporting on his remarks said he tied the half-point idea to October core inflation running around 0.3% or higher, which is what the data showed. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan went further, saying two more increases will be needed to bring inflation down.

According to CME FedWatch figures cited by Eurasia Business News, a 25-basis-point hike in December is fully priced in, with roughly a 13.6% chance of a 50-basis-point move. The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75%-4.00% at its late-October meeting, per Fortune. One analyst told TheStreet that the bigger open question is whether the Fed hikes again in January.
money: Variable-rate debt such as credit cards and home-equity lines will likely get more expensive after a hike; paying down the highest-rate balance first is a common move.
If a 0.25 to 0.50 point increase lands, high-yield savings and money-market rates usually follow upward within weeks.
Anyone planning to borrow, refinance or lock a rate before December can ask lenders about lock options and compare offers on the same day.
Savers can consider short-term CDs or Treasury bills to lock current yields, weighing the risk that rates rise further.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Meets Valuation Pushback: Reports Point to About $1.5 Trillion, Down From a $2 Trillion Ceiling
stories.deck: Investors want a bigger discount after a tech selloff; the updated filing left October revenue blank, one report says.
stories.summary: Anthropic's S-1 went public Oct. 26; sources I read cite roughly $1.4-1.5T valuation talk, but pricing details were not confirmed.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting.

A KuCoin blog post dated Nov. 6 says Anthropic released its Form S-1 publicly on Oct. 26 and that underwriters narrowed valuation talk from a $2.0 trillion ceiling to about $1.42-1.50 trillion after pushback from institutional investors in closed-door meetings. It reports revenue of $33.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026, including $16.8 billion in the third quarter, plus a quarterly operating loss and compute commitments of up to about $895 billion. The post itself warns that some of its figures do not reconcile and should be checked against the SEC filing.

Finimize, in a Nov. 5 article, says some investors want a larger IPO discount after the tech selloff and were uneasy that an updated filing left October revenue blank. It describes a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation as one some buyers see as a ceiling, and says the roadshow could slow if markets or disclosures lag. Neither source gave a confirmed pricing date or final share price, so those details remain unconfirmed here.
money: Retail investors can usually only get IPO shares through brokers that offer allocations; first-day pops are not guaranteed and large IPOs have often traded below their first-day highs.
If you own index funds, a mega-listing can eventually add a new large holding, so check what share of your fund sits in AI-related names.
Treat third-party valuation numbers with caution and read the company's own filing before making decisions.
A cooling AI-stock mood, if it persists, can affect tech-heavy retirement funds; rebalancing once a year is a simple discipline.

sources.t: Anthropic IPO valuation pushback amid November 2026 market selloff (KuCoin blog)
Anthropic's IPO roadshow is running into valuation pushback (Finimize)

stories.headline: Tuesday Movers: PepGen +93%, ZipRecruiter +54%, Digital Turbine -36%, Take-Two +8% on GTA VI Orders, and Costco Declares a $30 Special Dividend
stories.deck: Earnings reports drove the big single-stock swings on a down day for the indexes.
stories.summary: Biggest regular-session moves: PepGen +92.89%, ZipRecruiter +53.61%, Digital Turbine -35.84%, Groupon -23.05%; Costco special dividend after hours.
paras: Among the sharpest regular-session moves, PepGen jumped 92.89% on trial results for a rare muscle disease drug, ZipRecruiter rose 53.61% after earnings, Ameresco gained 23.03% with a record $7.2 billion project backlog, and Securitize rose 22.88% on a deal to buy River One and a $50 million buyback. On the downside, Digital Turbine fell 35.84% after results despite raising its revenue forecast, Groupon fell 23.05%, Gilat Satellite fell 20.45% and Paysign fell 18.94%.

Take-Two rose 8.31%, with the company pointing to strong pre-orders for GTA VI, according to KuCoin News. Microsoft slid 2.38% and Caterpillar 2.39% in the Dow. After the close, Costco declared a special dividend of $30 per share, and Rigetti Computing fell 8.40% after its results. AAA's national average gas price dropped below $4 a gallon for the first time since July.
money: A special dividend is taxable income in a regular brokerage account; the amount for each shareholder depends on shares owned on the record date.
Single-stock swings of 20-90% in a day show why diversified funds are the common way to limit the risk of one earnings surprise.
Gas under $4 nationally is a small relief; California prices differ, so a local app comparison can still save a few cents per gallon.
Avoid chasing stocks after a big one-day jump, since follow-through is far from assured.

stories.headline: Oil Settles at Lowest Since Aug. 31 as Trump Holds Off on Iran Strikes, Gold Drops 2.6%, and U.S. Gas Falls Below $4
stories.deck: Brent closed at $91.49 and WTI at $86.04 after last week's record slide in crude.
stories.summary: Brent $91.49 (-1.17%), WTI $86.04; spot gold about $4,032 (-2.6%) in late trading; AAA gas under $4.
paras: Brent crude for January delivery settled at $91.49, down 1.17%, and WTI for December settled at $86.04, down 0.93%, both the lowest settlements since Aug. 31, after President Trump said he would hold off on new strikes against Iran. Last week Brent fell 16.42% to $98.32, its largest weekly drop since 2020, according to a Mitrade weekly report, which also cited advancing U.S.-Iran talks, OPEC+ holding December output flat and weak U.S. demand growth.

Spot gold fell about 2.6% to roughly $4,032 an ounce in late U.S. trading, and silver dropped about 3.55% to $51.41, after gold had gained 4.51% last week to $4,074.90. AAA's national average gas price slipped below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, StockTitan reported.
money: Lower crude generally filters to pump prices with a lag of days to weeks; fill up gradually rather than all at once if prices keep falling.
Gold is down sharply in a day; anyone buying physical gold should compare dealer premiums over spot, which can be significant.
Airline fares and delivery costs are partly tied to fuel; booking holiday travel with flexible-cancellation fares can capture later price drops.
If crude rebounds on Iran news, energy-heavy funds will move the other way, which is one reason broad funds beat chasing headlines.

Weekly Report: Gold up 4.5%, Brent down 16.4% (Mitrade)

stories.headline: Mortgage Rates Had Fallen to About 7.05%, the Lowest Since September, but the 10-Year Yield's Jump to 5% Clouds the Outlook
stories.deck: Fortune's rate tracker showed the average 30-year fixed at 7.046% on Nov. 6, down from 7.176% a week earlier.
stories.summary: 30-year fixed averaged 7.046% (Nov. 6); the 10-year yield rose to about 5.0% on Nov. 10.
paras: Fortune, using Mortgage Research Center data, reported the average 30-year fixed conventional rate at 7.046% on Nov. 6, down from 7.085% the day before and 7.176% a week earlier. The Mortgage Bankers Association said rates had drifted to their lowest level since September, though applications dipped 1.2% for the week ending Oct. 30. FHA loans averaged 6.549% and VA loans 6.614%.

The following Tuesday, the 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.0% after the hot inflation report, according to TheStreet and Eurasia Business News. Mortgage rates do not track the Fed's rate directly, but they often move with Treasury yields, so the early-week jump is a reason borrowers should expect pressure on rates in the coming days, though the exact effect is not yet measured.
money: Shopping at least three lenders on the same day can save thousands over the life of a loan; rates differ by lender.
If you are close to buying, ask about a rate lock with a float-down option so you can benefit if rates fall.
FHA and VA rates were lower than conventional in this survey, which can matter for first-time and veteran buyers.
Paying points is only worth it if you will hold the loan long enough to recoup the upfront cost.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Hovers Near $74,500: ETF Outflows of About $1.3 Billion and a Key Support Level Just Above $73,000
stories.deck: The coin has no crypto-specific catalyst and is trading as a proxy for risk appetite, one report says.
stories.summary: Bitcoin was $74,549 on Monday morning (-1.67% in 24 hours); about 40% below its record.
paras: Fortune reported Bitcoin at $74,549.48 at 7:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 9, down 1.67% from the previous morning. InvestingLive described the move as risk-sentiment driven, noting Nvidia's headlines and Middle East tension, and said U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw outflows of nearly $1.3 billion in the five sessions to Nov. 6. The coin is down about 3% on the week and 8% on the month, roughly 40% below its record high.

The analyst commentary highlighted the 200-day moving average just above $73,000 as support and the 50-day average near $82,000 as resistance. I did not find a verified Bitcoin quote for Tuesday or Wednesday, so Monday's reading is the latest confirmed number.
money: Crypto has been trading with tech stocks recently, so it may not diversify a portfolio as much as hoped.
Dollar-cost averaging, buying a fixed amount on a schedule, is the common way to limit the risk of buying a peak.
Crypto gains and losses are taxable events in the U.S.; keeping a record of purchase dates and prices simplifies tax time.
Only money you can afford to see fall sharply is suitable for such a volatile asset.

sources.t: Price of Bitcoin, Nov. 9, 2026 (Fortune)
Bitcoin continues to trade heavily, under $74,600 (InvestingLive)

stories.headline: The Money Calendar: Treasury Auction and Housing Data Thursday, PPI Friday, Tariff Dates Dec. 4 and Jan. 1, Fed Dec. 8-9, Funding Cliff Dec. 11
stories.deck: A date-by-date guide to the events most likely to move markets, rates and household bills.
stories.summary: Key dates: Nov. 12 home sales and 30-year auction, Nov. 13 PPI, Dec. 8-9 Fed, Dec. 11 funding deadline, Dec. 31 Covered California, Jan. 1 wage and tariff changes.
paras: This week: Wednesday Nov. 11 is Veterans Day, with stocks open and the bond market closed. Thursday Nov. 12 brings U.S. existing home sales at 10 a.m. ET, a 30-year Treasury auction, remarks by Fed Governor Barr, and Nebius earnings before the open. Friday Nov. 13 brings the October producer price index. Separately, three House committee chairmen have asked Nvidia's CEO for a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 and requested a reply by Nov. 11.

Next: Polysilicon tariffs under Section 232 take effect Dec. 4. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9. Federal funding runs out Dec. 11 unless Congress acts. Dec. 31 is the deadline to pick a Covered California plan for full-year coverage. On Jan. 1, California's minimum wage rises to $17.40 and furniture and cabinet tariff rates step up. China's trade-truce measures run to Jan. 10, and Covered California enrollment ends Jan. 31.
money: Mark the Dec. 31 Covered California date; picking a plan late can leave a gap in coverage.
Auction results and PPI can move mortgage and savings rates, so rate-lock decisions may benefit from checking them.
Big-ticket furniture or cabinet purchases may be cheaper before the Jan. 1 tariff step-up, though prices at retailers depend on stock and contracts.
Employers and workers in California can plan now for the Jan. 1 pay changes.

stories.headline: China Extends Its Pause on Tariffs and Rare-Earth Curbs for Two Months, to Jan. 10, Ahead of a Trump-Xi Meeting
stories.deck: A 24% extra tariff on U.S. goods stays suspended while a 10% levy remains; the U.S. extends 178 exclusions.
stories.summary: The truce due to expire Nov. 10 now runs to Jan. 10; Trump and Xi are expected to meet at APEC next week.
paras: China said it will keep suspending a 24% additional tariff on U.S. goods for two months, while a 10% tariff stays in place, extending a truce that was due to expire Tuesday. Export-control waivers on certain critical minerals and technologies, suspended measures against 11 U.S. firms on its unreliable entities list and 16 on its export control list, and a pause on special port fees on U.S.-linked vessels all run to Jan. 10, 2027, according to gCaptain.

On the U.S. side, filings cited by The National say the U.S. is suspending action in a Section 301 probe of China's maritime and logistics sectors and extending 178 tariff exclusions for Chinese goods. Treasury Secretary Bessent and trade representative Greer pressed China to fully implement the Busan commitments on rare earths, farm purchases and other minerals. Trump and Xi are expected to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week.
money: The pause lowers near-term risk of a sudden spike in prices of electronics, batteries and magnets that rely on Chinese minerals, but the Jan. 10 date is another cliff.
Importers can use the extension window to confirm their tariff classification and exclusion eligibility.
Farm-state exporters and soybean buyers watch China purchases; commodity prices can react to the summit.
Consumers buying big-ticket imported goods should expect price stability only through winter, not beyond.

China Extends US Trade Truce by Two Months (gCaptain)

stories.headline: Tariffs by the Calendar: Polysilicon Dec. 4, Furniture and Kitchen Cabinets Step Up Jan. 1, Drone Parts Feb. 9
stories.deck: A tracker lists the scheduled changes; robotics and wind-turbine actions come with status reports in April.
stories.summary: Furniture rates rise to 30% (upholstered wood) and 50% (cabinets and vanities) on Jan. 1; polysilicon tariffs start Dec. 4.
paras: The Trade Compliance Resource Hub's Nov. 3 tracker lists these dates: Section 232 polysilicon tariffs take effect Dec. 4, with minimum import prices and rates of 10% for the UK and 15% for the EU, Japan and other countries. The 25% rate on furniture and cabinets from other countries applies through Dec. 31, then rises on Jan. 1, 2027 to 30% for upholstered wooden furniture and 50% for kitchen cabinets and vanities. A 25% rate on certain drone components takes effect Feb. 9, 2027.

Status reports for wind turbines (April 20, 2027) and robotics and industrial machinery (April 26, 2027) are due to the president, with rates still to be determined. A Nicaragua Section 301 rate rises to 10% on Jan. 1, 2027. The tracker itself advises checking the Federal Register for official dates.
money: Anyone remodeling a kitchen or buying upholstered furniture soon may prefer to order before Jan. 1, though retailer pricing may already reflect expected increases.
Solar installers and buyers could see equipment costs shift after Dec. 4; quotes can be compared for price validity dates.
Small businesses that import can ask a customs broker about classification and timing.
Tariffs are paid at import, so effects on shelf prices often show up weeks or months later.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker, Nov. 3 update (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)
China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months (The National)

stories.headline: Tariff Refunds: Only Importers of Record Can Claim, and the Section 122 Tariffs Remain in Legal Limbo
stories.deck: Customs says refunds arrive roughly 60 to 90 days after acceptance, but compliance questions can delay them.
stories.summary: CBP's CAPE refund process launched April 20; the Court of International Trade declared the Section 122 proclamation invalid May 7 but collection continues pending appeal.
paras: According to the Nov. 3 tracker, U.S. Customs launched the CAPE refund process on April 20, 2026 for duties collected under the emergency tariffs struck down by courts. Only the importer of record or broker who filed the original entries can apply. CAPE accepts unliquidated entries and some recently liquidated ones, and CBP expects refunds generally within 60 to 90 days of acceptance. The government is appealing a court order on finally liquidated entries.

The tracker also says the Court of International Trade declared the Section 122 proclamation invalid on May 7, 2026, but did not issue a universal injunction, so collection continues while the government appeals. China's commerce side has said it believes the U.S. intends to rely on Section 301 tariffs to replace the invalidated emergency tariffs, per gCaptain. The sources I read gave no dollar totals for refunds paid.
money: Consumers generally have no direct claim; the refund goes to the importer of record, so any pass-through to buyers depends on the business.
Small businesses that imported goods should check whether their broker filed claims and keep entry records.
Companies receiving refunds may report one-time gains, which can move earnings; look at earnings notes for 'tariff refund' line items.
Stay skeptical of offers to 'recover your tariff costs' for a fee; confirm eligibility with a licensed customs broker.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker, Nov. 3 update (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)

stories.headline: Trump Holds Off on New Iran Strikes but Keeps the Hormuz Blockade; Talks Are Alive, but No Breakthrough Is Near
stories.deck: Qatar's prime minister met Trump and Vance; Rubio says Iran's conditions are unrealistic as tanker attacks continue.
stories.summary: Trump paused new strikes 'for the time being'; Brent fell to $91.49; Iran's proposal and U.S. demands remain far apart.
paras: President Trump said he plans to hold off on new strikes against Iran for the time being after appeals from Gulf states and a White House meeting with Qatar's prime minister, but he will keep the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported via Al-Monitor. The war began Feb. 28, a June truce collapsed, and attacks on tankers have continued at the highest rate since the war began, according to the report. Secretary of State Rubio said a breakthrough is not imminent.

Al Jazeera reported that Iran offered a new proposal through Qatari mediators on Nov. 6, but says it will discuss it only after the U.S. meets seven demands, including sanctions relief, restored oil waivers and recognition of a new Hormuz route. The IAEA says Iran holds 440.9 kg of uranium enriched up to 60%. Markets reacted to the pause: Brent settled at $91.49 Tuesday, its lowest settlement since Aug. 31, per Eurasia Business News.
money: Oil has been the main channel to your wallet; crude is down sharply from last week, but a breakdown in talks could reverse it quickly.
Travelers may see fuel-related airfares ease if crude stays lower, though fares also reflect holiday demand.
Gas near $4 nationally gives drivers a bit of room, but California typically runs above the national average.
Energy and defense stocks react in opposite directions to peace headlines, which is a reason not to chase either.

stories.headline: Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. Meet in Abu Dhabi: Security Guarantees Top the Agenda, but Analysts Expect No Peace Deal
stories.deck: It is the first trilateral round in nine months; technical issues like grain and energy ceasefires could come up.
stories.summary: Trilateral talks run Nov. 10-11; no accord is expected; Russia says it will not drop its Donbas goal.
paras: Delegations from Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10, scheduled to run through Nov. 11, with Witkoff and Kushner for the U.S., Umerov for Ukraine and Medinsky for Russia. Russia's foreign minister said security issues come first, and the U.S. side has described the aim as discussing postwar security directly. Meduza reports Putin told Nordic leaders Russia will not give up capturing all of Donbas, while European governments are not part of the trilateral format.

Al Jazeera's preview says analysts are pessimistic about tangible progress, though technical topics such as grain supplies, Black Sea and energy ceasefires and another prisoner exchange could be discussed. The sources I read were published before the talks ended, so outcomes are not yet known.
money: A grain or Black Sea deal would matter for wheat and food prices; a collapse of talks tends to lift energy and wheat prices.
European energy and defense shares react to headlines; consider how much such themes already sit in your funds.
Higher global fuel prices feed into U.S. diesel and shipping costs, which pass through to grocery prices.
Expect headline volatility; a plan that does not depend on a peace deal timing is more robust.

sources.t: Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. to hold peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10 (Meduza)
'No concession': What to expect from Russia-US-Ukraine talks (Al Jazeera)

stories.headline: Shutdown Clock: Funding Expires Dec. 11, and as of Nov. 3 the House Had Passed Only 3 of 12 Spending Bills and the Senate None
stories.deck: Congress returned Nov. 9 with a month to pass full-year bills or another stopgap.
stories.summary: Stopgap H.R. 6500 funds most agencies through Dec. 11; a lapse would start Dec. 12.
paras: The stopgap law H.R. 6500, which the House passed 370-48 on Sept. 1 and the president signed the next day, funds most agencies through Dec. 11, according to AACOM and Multibagg. As of Nov. 3 the House had passed three of the 12 regular spending bills and the Senate none, and most bills need 60 Senate votes. The outgoing Congress can pass full-year bills, a shorter stopgap into early 2027, or a mix, and the new Congress is sworn in Jan. 3.

Multibagg also notes the Fed meets Dec. 8-9, two days before the deadline, that health center funding expires Dec. 31 and may be attached to a deal, and that the country had a 43-day shutdown from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025.
money: Federal workers and contractors can build a cash buffer of a few weeks of expenses now, since pay can be delayed during a lapse.
Check which services you rely on (passport, nutrition programs, national parks); some continue and some pause during a lapse.
Past shutdowns have had mixed effects on the stock market, per Multibagg, so avoid reacting to headlines.
If you depend on a federally funded health center, watch the Dec. 31 funding date.

sources.t: The 11 December Funding Deadline (Multibagg)
President Trump signs continuing resolution to fund government through Dec. 11 (AACOM)

stories.headline: 2027 Tax Numbers Are Set: Standard Deduction $16,600 Single and $33,200 Joint, Child Credit $2,300, Gift Exclusion $20,000
stories.deck: The IRS inflation adjustments cover nearly 70 provisions, including the brackets and health FSA limit.
stories.summary: Top 37% bracket starts at $661,375 single; Health FSA limit $3,500; child credit $2,300 ($1,800 refundable).
paras: The IRS's Revenue Procedure 2026-35 sets the 2027 standard deduction at $16,600 for single filers, $33,200 for married couples filing jointly and $24,925 for heads of household. The 22% bracket starts at $52,025 for single filers and $104,050 for joint filers, and the 37% bracket starts at $661,375 and $793,650.

The maximum child tax credit is $2,300 with up to $1,800 refundable, the earned income credit maxes at $8,496 for three or more children, the annual gift exclusion rises to $20,000, the estate tax exclusion to $15.48 million and the health FSA limit to $3,500. These apply to 2027 income, not the return due this spring. The articles did not list retirement account contribution limits.
money: Year-end planning for 2026 uses this year's numbers; the 2027 figures matter for withholding changes and next year's budget.
A higher FSA cap of $3,500 means you can set aside more pre-tax money for medical costs starting in 2027.
Bracket thresholds rising with inflation means a raise that only matches inflation should not push many people into a higher bracket.
A tax professional can say how the numbers affect your situation; these are general figures.

sources.t: IRS Adjusts Tax Brackets, Standard Deduction for Tax Year 2027 (CPA Practice Advisor)
IRS sets inflation adjustments for tax year 2027 (Accounting Today)

stories.headline: California FAIR Plan Rates Rise 29.1% on Average for 675,000+ Customers; Some Wildfire Premiums Could Double
stories.deck: The state's insurer of last resort says its exposure is $768 billion against a cash balance of $200-400 million.
stories.summary: The increase applies to renewals on or after Oct. 15; some homes near high-risk areas may see far bigger jumps.
paras: The California FAIR Plan's 29.1% average increase took effect Oct. 15 and applies to existing policies at renewal on or after that date, affecting more than 675,000 customers, KQED reports. The Plan had asked for 35.8%. Homes in high wildfire-risk areas may see premiums roughly double, while lower-risk policyholders and some urban customers may see less, or even reductions.

A Stanford study found California homeowners' premiums are up 84% since 2020, and FAIR Plan enrollment has gone from under 2% to 5% of homes. KQED says new business at the Plan is down 25% from last year and traditional insurers are writing in California again, so some policyholders may be able to move to private coverage.
money: Ask an independent agent for quotes from private insurers before your FAIR Plan renewal; more companies are writing policies again, per KQED.
The FAIR Plan covers fire but not all perils; ask about a companion 'difference in conditions' policy.
Wildfire mitigation such as defensible space and ember-resistant vents can lower premiums with some insurers.
Keep a home inventory with photos for claims.

sources.t: California FAIR Plan announces 29.1% rate hike (KQED)
California FAIR Plan customers face 29% average rate hike (KMPH)

stories.headline: California's Minimum Wage Rises to $17.40 on Jan. 1, and the Exempt Salary Floor Hits $72,384
stories.deck: The increase from $16.90 is the highest state minimum in the nation; fast-food ($20) and health-care ($25) rates are separate.
stories.summary: Statewide minimum wage of $17.40 from Jan. 1, 2027; exempt salary threshold $72,384; local rates may be higher.
paras: The Department of Industrial Relations says California's statewide minimum wage will rise to $17.40 an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, up from $16.90, after the Department of Finance certified the adjustment on July 31. The salary threshold for most overtime-exempt employees rises to $72,384 a year, twice the minimum wage for a full-time schedule.

KTVU notes California has the highest state minimum wage in the nation, nearly 2.5 times the federal $7.25, and that fast food workers have a $20 wage and health care workers $25. Some cities and counties set higher minimums, and employers must pay the higher local rate.
money: Workers paid hourly can check January paychecks against the new rate; the Labor Commissioner's helpline is 833-526-4636.
Salaried workers earning below $72,384 may no longer be exempt from overtime.
Small businesses can budget now for payroll and for price adjustments.
A higher minimum wage can lift prices at labor-heavy businesses such as restaurants.

stories.headline: Nvidia Falls 5.5% as Its Board Probes Reports About Its CEO; Market Value Dips Below $4 Trillion Intraday
stories.deck: Independent directors hired outside counsel; three House chairs want a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18.
stories.summary: Nvidia closed down 5.47% Tuesday, its second straight drop; the board says it has no reason to think national security or confidential information was compromised.
paras: Nvidia shares closed down 5.47% Tuesday, and CNBC said the drop pulled down all three major indexes, per StockTitan and KuCoin. The company's market value briefly fell below $4 trillion during the day and was about $4.07 trillion at the close, its lowest since late March. The independent board members retained Joon H. Kim and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz for the investigation.

The probe follows an Oct. 29 New York Times report on a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which eeNews Europe says alleged links to Chinese intelligence. The board announced the inquiry on Nov. 8 and said it has no reason to believe national security or confidential Nvidia information was compromised. Three House committee chairmen asked for a Nov. 18 briefing and a reply by Nov. 11. Public information does not establish that secrets were passed or chips diverted, the article notes.
money: Nvidia is a large holding in many index funds, so a single-stock slide can touch retirement accounts even if you do not own it directly.
Investigations tend to create headline volatility rather than clear signals; avoid trading on rumor.
Check your fund's top holdings for concentration in a few AI companies.
If you hold individual shares, consider position size relative to your total portfolio.

sources.t: NVIDIA board investigation (eeNews Europe)
The Stock Market Today, November 10, 2026 (StockTitan)
U.S. stocks decline as October CPI exceeds expectations; Nvidia drops 5.5% (KuCoin News)

stories.headline: CoreWeave Beats Estimates and Raises 2026 Revenue Guidance to $13-13.3 Billion; Nebius Reports Thursday
stories.deck: Third-quarter revenue was $3.66 billion; shares rose after hours, by 2.6% to 8% depending on the source.
stories.summary: Q3 revenue $3.66B vs $3.55B expected; adjusted loss $0.95/share vs $1.16 expected.
paras: CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion against $3.55 billion expected and an adjusted loss of $0.95 per share against a $1.16 loss expected, KuCoin News reported. It raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13 billion to $13.3 billion. Shares rose in after-hours trading, about 8% in one report and 2.59% in another from StockTitan.

StockHub's preview said investors were watching capital spending, interest expense and operating cash flow at AI-cloud companies, with Nebius reporting Thursday before the open. The same page noted the Philadelphia chip index had fallen 12.15% over seven days through Nov. 6 and the VIX stood at 25.64.
money: AI-infrastructure results are a gauge for chip and power stocks; heavy debt-funded spending makes these firms sensitive to interest rates.
After-hours moves often shrink or reverse by the next day's close.
Broad funds already hold these names in small slices.
Watch cash flow and debt, not just revenue, when judging this group.

stories.deck: Analysts cite money moving into defensive sectors; AMD, Broadcom and Lam Research each rose more than 7% Tuesday.
stories.summary: SOX -12.15% over seven days to 9,390.25 (Nov. 6); VIX 25.64; a Nov. 6 blog says OpenAI cut its private raise Oct. 30.
paras: StockHub reported the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.15% over seven days to 9,390.25 at the Nov. 6 close, with the VIX at 25.64. On Tuesday one analyst told TheStreet money was moving out of AI names into defensive sectors such as healthcare, while KuCoin News reported AMD up 7.25%, Broadcom up 7.86% and Lam Research up 8.48%.

A KuCoin blog post says OpenAI cut its planned private raise from $30 billion to $20 billion and its pre-money valuation from $1.40 trillion to $1.25 trillion on Oct. 30, and that Alphabet fell 12.6% in a day on Oct. 29. That blog warns some figures need checking against filings, so treat those numbers cautiously.
money: Chip swings of 10% in a week show why a diversified fund spreads the risk.
Healthcare and other defensive sectors tend to hold up better in selloffs but can lag in rallies.
If your 401(k) is a target-date fund, it already rebalances for you.
Avoid timing the AI cycle; steady contributions have been a more reliable approach.

stories.headline: AI's Power Appetite Reaches Regulators: FERC Weighs Who Pays for Grid Upgrades as Data Centers Approach 4-5% of U.S. Electricity
stories.deck: EPRI projects 10-20% of demand by 2035; Virginia is already near 25%.
stories.summary: A FERC proposal asks whether large loads should pay full upgrade costs; sources describe rising power prices in the PJM region.
paras: Fierce Network reports that a FERC proposed rulemaking (docket RM26-4-000) would set 60-day interconnection study timelines for customers willing to curtail usage and asks whether large loads should pay the full cost of grid upgrades. It cites EPRI estimates that data centers account for about 4-5% of U.S. electricity demand today, with 10-20% expected by 2035, and Virginia at roughly 25% already. The article is undated, so check timing.

A May 17 repost said PJM's independent market monitor attributed a 76% rise in average prices to data-center load and asked FERC to make large tech companies pay for the upgrades they trigger; the post has unnamed sourcing and caveats. California's situation is different, but the debate over who pays for AI's power is spreading.
money: Ask your utility about time-of-use plans; shifting laundry and EV charging off-peak can cut bills.
Rate-case notices can be commented on; many state commissions accept public input.
Home efficiency upgrades are a hedge against rising power prices.
Utility and power-equipment stocks have been tied to the AI trade, so they can fall with it.

sources.t: AI power demand hits regulatory tipping point (Fierce Network)
PJM power prices spike 76% as watchdog demands tech giants pay (DEV Community repost)

stories.headline: Covered California Open Enrollment Runs to Jan. 31, With State Help for Incomes up to 200% of Poverty and 55% of Enrollees Seeing No Premium Rise
stories.deck: State subsidy funding rises to $300 million; about 200,000 become newly eligible for help.
stories.summary: Pick a plan by Dec. 31 for full-year coverage; 1.7 million are enrolled; the center is closed Veterans Day.
paras: Covered California's open enrollment runs Nov. 1 through Jan. 31, 2027, and enrollees must pick a plan by Dec. 31 to be covered all year. State subsidy funding rises from $190 million in 2026 to $300 million, extending extra help to incomes up to 200% of the poverty level, about $31,920 for one person or $66,000 for a family of four. About 55% of current enrollees will see no premium increase, nearly 200,000 can choose between two $0 Silver plans and more than 330,000 will pay less.

The state says its subsidy cannot replace the roughly $2.5 billion a year lost when federal enhanced premium tax credits expired. An estimated 1.1 million-plus uninsured Californians are eligible, 461,000 for Covered California help and 682,000 for Medi-Cal. Free enrollment help is available at (800) 300-1506, Monday-Friday 8-6, and the center is closed Nov. 11.
money: Compare plans even if you plan to keep your current one; premiums and networks change each year.
Check Medi-Cal eligibility if your income is low; it can mean $0 coverage.
Picking by Dec. 31 avoids a coverage gap in January.
Free certified enrollers can help at no cost; avoid anyone who charges.

sources.t: Covered California 2027 open enrollment, press release
Covered California kicks off 2027 open enrollment

stories.headline: CalFresh Work Rules: Adults 18-64 Without Dependents Must Show 20 Hours a Week to Keep Benefits Beyond Three Months
stories.deck: Reports differ on how many could lose aid; one projects about 562,000 over a year.
stories.summary: Rules began June 1 per KTVU; a San Diego outlet says requirements take effect in October; check with your county.
paras: KTVU reports the federal work rules began June 1, 2026 for adults 18 to 64 without dependents: to keep more than three months of benefits in three years, they must average 20 hours of work weekly, earn at least $217.50 a week, or join an approved training or community engagement program. Adults 55 to 64 and people experiencing homelessness are newly included unless exempt. Exemptions include disability, a child under 14, pregnancy and health conditions, and seven counties under a waiver.

Times of San Diego reports about 47,000 people could lose CalFresh starting in October and that an assemblymember's office projects about 562,000 over a year, while about 3.4 million households are still expected to receive CalFresh. The two sources give different start timing, so confirm your own date with your county.
money: Call your county social services office to document hours or ask about exemptions.
Keep pay stubs or volunteer logs.
If you lose benefits, food banks can bridge the gap.
Ask about waivers and exemptions before assuming you are affected.

sources.t: New CalFresh work requirements start June 1 (KTVU)
As many as 47,000 people could be kicked off CalFresh (Times of San Diego)

stories.headline: MyFirstEV: Up to $3,500 Off a First Electric Vehicle, Applied at the Dealership, With Nearly 12,000 Buyers So Far
stories.deck: Used EVs qualify for $1,750; price caps are $50,000 new and $25,000 used.
stories.summary: The state committed $135.5 million, matched by automakers for about $271 million; no application after purchase.
paras: Electrive reports California's MyFirstEV program gives first-time zero-emission vehicle buyers $3,500 off a new vehicle priced at $50,000 or less and $1,750 off a used one priced at $25,000 or less, sold through a manufacturer's pre-owned program. It is applied at the point of sale, so buyers do not file for reimbursement. Nearly 12,000 buyers have used it since the August launch.

The state committed $135.5 million, matched by participating automakers for about $271 million. Engadget says only full battery vehicles qualify, not hybrids, and lists the Leaf, Model 3, Model Y, Ioniq 5 and Mustang Mach-E as examples but did not confirm each trim meets the cap. Electrive says hybrids are included; the two sources conflict, so ask the dealer.
money: Ask the dealer to confirm eligibility in writing and whether the discount is already in the quoted price.
Compare with other incentives like utility EV rates and charger rebates.
Funds are limited and first-come; the program could close once money runs out.
Factor in home-charging installation costs.

sources.t: Nearly 12,000 Californians switch to EVs thanks to MyFirstEV (Electrive)
California's MyFirstEV provides a $3,500 instant rebate (Engadget)

stories.headline: Social Security Rises 3.6% in January, About $75 a Month for the Average Retiree, but Medicare Premiums Will Take a Bite
stories.deck: The Part B premium is projected to rise $6.60 to $209.50; official figure expected this month.
stories.summary: The COLA is the largest in four years; the taxable maximum rises to $192,300.
paras: Social Security benefits rise 3.6% in January, the largest raise in several years, adding about $75 a month for the average retired worker and about $59 for disability and survivor beneficiaries, according to IBTimes and the Star-Advertiser. The maximum earnings subject to payroll tax rises to $192,300 from $184,500.

The Medicare trustees project the standard Part B premium rising from $202.90 to $209.50 a month, which would leave the average retiree's net gain near $68.40 a month. CMS is expected to confirm the number in November. The Part D deductible is projected to rise from $615 to $700 and the out-of-pocket limit from $2,100 to $2,400.
money: Review Medicare plans during open enrollment; plan prices and drug coverage change each year.
Low-income seniors may qualify for Medicare Savings Programs that cover Part B premiums.
Budget for the net raise, not the headline COLA.
Higher earners should note the new payroll-tax cap for 2027.

sources.t: Social Security says retirees will get a 3.6% raise (Star-Advertiser)
Social Security's 2027 COLA rises 3.6% (IBTimes)
